purpose: Introduce quantum computing and why it exists
math_required: Basic probability; complex numbers only lightly (amplitudes).
learning_objectives: Define quantum computing in one or two sentences.
Explain why it exists, including simulation of nature and problems that scale badly classically.
Distinguish a classical bit from a qubit, including what measurement does.
Describe superposition, interference and entanglement in plain language and state a common misconception about each.
State that quantum computers give speedups only for particular problems and are not general replacements.
Name noise/decoherence as a major obstacle and explain NISQ.
Calculate measurement probabilities for a simple one-qubit state.

concepts.title: Quantum computing
concepts.definition: A model of computation in which information is held in quantum systems (qubits) and processed by controlled quantum operations (gates), followed by measurement.
concepts.explanation: Quantum computers use quantum-mechanical properties to tackle certain problems that can be difficult for classical computers. They are specialized tools rather than universal replacements for classical computers.

concepts.title: Classical bit
concepts.definition: A classical bit has a value of 0 or 1.
concepts.explanation: A classical bit can be pictured as a switch that is off (0) or on (1).

concepts.title: Qubit
concepts.definition: A qubit is the basic unit of quantum information and can be described by a state α|0⟩ + β|1⟩, with |α|² + |β|² = 1.
concepts.explanation: A qubit can have a superposition of the computational basis states. Measurement in that basis gives 0 or 1 according to the corresponding probabilities.

concepts.title: Superposition
concepts.definition: A quantum state can be a combination of basis states.
concepts.explanation: Superposition is not simply a hidden classical value. The amplitudes of the component basis states determine measurement probabilities.

concepts.title: Measurement
concepts.definition: Measurement of a qubit in the computational basis yields 0 or 1 with probabilities determined by the squared magnitudes of its amplitudes.
concepts.explanation: After a measurement result is obtained, the state is projected onto the observed basis state in the examples covered here.

concepts.title: Probability amplitudes
concepts.definition: For |ψ⟩ = α|0⟩ + β|1⟩, α and β are amplitudes and their squared magnitudes give measurement probabilities.

concepts.title: Interference
concepts.definition: Quantum amplitudes can add constructively or destructively.
concepts.explanation: Quantum algorithms can arrange interference so amplitudes for unwanted outcomes cancel while useful outcomes are amplified.

concepts.title: Entanglement
concepts.definition: Entanglement creates quantum correlations between qubits that cannot be described as independent states.
concepts.explanation: Entangled measurement results can be strongly correlated. Entanglement does not provide faster-than-light communication.

concepts.title: Quantum circuit
concepts.definition: A quantum circuit is a sequence of quantum operations or gates applied to qubits, followed by measurement.
concepts.explanation: A circuit can be viewed as initialize → apply gates → measure, with repeated shots used to obtain outcome statistics.

concepts.title: Decoherence
concepts.definition: Decoherence is loss of quantum coherence through interaction with the environment.
concepts.explanation: Noise and environmental interaction make quantum states difficult to preserve and are major engineering obstacles.

concepts.title: NISQ
concepts.definition: NISQ stands for Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum.
concepts.explanation: The term describes the era of quantum devices that are noisy and intermediate in scale, before large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computing.

concepts.title: Problem-specific speedup
concepts.definition: Quantum computers can provide advantages for particular computational problems; they are not generally faster for every task.
concepts.explanation: The source emphasizes specialized use and hybrid workflows rather than replacing classical computers.

concepts.title: Hybrid quantum-classical computing
concepts.definition: A workflow in which classical and quantum resources divide computational tasks.
concepts.explanation: Classical computers remain important for many tasks, including everyday computing and classical post-processing.

concepts.title: Qubit technologies
concepts.definition: The source identifies implementations including superconducting circuits, trapped ions, quantum dots and photons.
concepts.explanation: Different hardware approaches have different engineering characteristics; hardware details beyond the Topic 1.1 scope should be treated cautiously.
